findings.finding: The lock-only candidate is structurally safe to adopt: package.json remains unchanged with @ai-matrx dependencies declared latest; the candidate only resolves rich-content 0.2.149 and rich-editor 0.5.104. Extension source has no direct imports or uses of changed/removed package APIs (including CopyMenuButton.copyRaw). I could not establish exact-candidate user behavior in the live extension.

Both published CHANGELOG entries claim metadata-only republishing and no consumer action, but the published dist differs materially: rich-content changes 21 emitted files, including copy menu/API changes, formatted copy, HTML page menu actions and selection copy; rich-editor changes four emitted files and adds visual-selection serialization used by editor selection sources. The Consumer-action gate correctly passes the declarations but does not validate the published runtime delta.

Because the extension mounts @ai-matrx/chat in PackageChatView, downstream chat/editor reachability is plausible; source inspection alone does not prove whether these changed rich-content/editor paths render there. Treat adoption as package-graph-safe, with product acceptance limited to chat copy menu defaults/Markdown-text-formatted rows, selection copy from visual and source editors, and HTML publish menu availability/absence under the extension host bindings.
